units.zh: 完顏奴申
units.en: Wanyan Nushen
units.literal: Wanyan Nushen

units.zh: 完顏奴申，字正甫，素蘭之弟也。
units.en: Wanyan Nushen, courtesy name Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Suluan.
units.literal: Wanyan Nushen, styled Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Suluan.

units.zh: 登策論進士第，仕曆清要。
units.en: He passed the Policy Discourse jinshi examination and rose through a series of prestigious offices.
units.literal: He passed the Presented Scholar examination in Policy Discourse and served in succession in posts of rank and importance.

units.zh: 正大三年八月，由翰林直學士充益政院說書官。
units.en: In the eighth month of Zhengda 3, while serving as a direct Hanlin academician, he was appointed lecturer at the Yizheng Court.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhengda, from Hanlin Academician Direct he was made Lecturer of the Yizheng Court.

units.zh: 五年，轉吏部侍郎。
units.en: In the fifth year he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 監察御史烏古論石魯剌劾近侍張文壽、仁壽、李麟之受敵帥饋遺，詔奴申鞫問，得其奸狀，上曲赦其罪，皆斥去，朝論快之。
units.en: Supervising censor Wugulun Shilula accused the emperor's close attendants Zhang Wenshou, Renshou, and Li Lin of accepting bribes from the enemy commander. The emperor ordered Nushen to investigate; when their misconduct was proved, he granted them a lenient pardon and had them all dismissed, to the satisfaction of court opinion.
units.literal: Supervising Censor Wugulun Shilula impeached the close attendants Zhang Wenshou, Renshou, and Li Lin for receiving gifts from the enemy commander; the emperor ordered Nushen to investigate, and when their treachery was established, the throne granted them lenient pardon for their crimes and all were dismissed—court opinion rejoiced.

units.zh: 九月，改侍講學士，以御史大夫奉使大元。
units.en: In the ninth month he was made court lecturer and sent to the Great Yuan as censor-in-chief on an embassy mission.
units.literal: In the ninth month he was changed to Court Lecturer and, as Censor-in-Chief, was sent on embassy to the Great Yuan.

units.zh: 至龍駒河，朝見太宗皇帝。
units.en: He reached the Longju River and had an audience with Emperor Taizong of the Yuan.
units.literal: He reached the Longju River and had audience with Emperor Taizong.

units.zh: 十二月，還。
units.en: He returned in the twelfth month.
units.literal: In the twelfth month he returned.

units.zh: 明年六月，遷吏部尚書，複往。
units.en: The following year, in the sixth month, he was promoted to minister of personnel and sent on another mission.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel and went again.

units.zh: 八年春，還。
units.en: He returned in the spring of the eighth year.
units.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he returned.

units.zh: 朝廷以勞拜參知政事。
units.en: In recognition of his service, the court appointed him vice grand councilor.
units.literal: The court, in recognition of his labors, appointed him Vice Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 天興元年春，大兵駐鄭州海灘寺，遣使招哀宗降。
units.en: In the spring of Tianxing 1, the Mongol army encamped at Haitansi in Zheng Prefecture and sent envoys urging Emperor Aizong to surrender.
units.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tianxing, the Great Army encamped at Haitansi in Zheng Prefecture and sent envoys to summon Emperor Aizong to surrender.

units.zh: 複以奴申往乞和。
units.en: Nushen was again dispatched to sue for peace.
units.literal: Nushen was again sent to beg for peace.

units.zh: 不許，攻汴益急。
units.en: The offer was refused, and the assault on Kaifeng intensified.
units.literal: They did not consent, and the assault on Bian grew fiercer.

units.zh: 汴受圍數月，倉庫匱乏，召武仙等入援不至，哀宗懼，以曹王訛可出質，請罷攻。
units.en: Kaifeng had been under siege for months, and the granaries were empty. Wuxian and others were called to relieve the city but never came. In fear, Emperor Aizong offered Prince Cao, Eke, as a hostage and asked that the assault be halted.
units.literal: Bian had been besieged for months; storehouses were exhausted; Wuxian and others were summoned to relieve the city but did not arrive; Emperor Aizong was afraid and offered Prince Cao, Eke, as hostage, requesting that the attack cease.

units.zh: 冬十月，哀宗議親出捍禦，以奴申參知政事、兼樞密副使，完顏習捏阿不樞密副使、兼知開封府、權參知政事，總諸軍留守京師。
units.en: In the tenth month of winter, Emperor Aizong planned to lead the defense in person. He left Nushen as vice grand councilor and concurrent vice commissioner of military affairs, and Wanyan Xinie Abu as vice commissioner of military affairs, concurrent prefect of Kaifeng, and acting vice grand councilor, to command all forces and hold the capital.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Emperor Aizong deliberated going out in person to resist; he made Nushen Vice Grand Councilor and concurrent Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Wanyan Xinie Abu Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrent Prefect of Kaifeng, and Acting Vice Grand Councilor, to command all armies and remain to guard the capital.

units.zh: 又以翰林學士承旨烏古孫卜吉提控諸王府，同判大睦親府事兼都點檢內族合周管宮掖事，左副點檢完顏阿撒、右副點檢溫敦阿裏副之，戶部尚書完顏珠顆兼裏城四面都總領，御史大夫裴滿阿虎帶兼鎮撫軍民都彈壓，諫議大夫近侍局使行省左右司郎中烏古孫奴申兼知宮省事。
units.en: He also appointed Hanlin academician-in-chief Wugusun Buji to oversee the princely mansions; inner clansman Hezhou, associate administrator of the Great Muxin princely establishment and chief inspector, to manage palace affairs, assisted by left deputy inspector Wanyan Asa and right deputy inspector Wendun Ali; minister of revenue Wanyan Zhuke as overall commander of the inner city's four sectors; censor-in-chief Peiman Ahudai as concurrent overall pacifier of army and people; and remonstrating censor and director of the close attendants bureau Wugusun Nushen, acting left and right bureau director of the branch secretariat, as concurrent administrator of palace affairs.
units.literal: He also appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Wugusun Buji to take charge of the princely mansions, concurrent Associate Administrator of the Great Muxin Princely Establishment and Chief Inspector; Inner Clansman Hezhou to manage palace affairs, with Left Deputy Inspector Wanyan Asa and Right Deputy Inspector Wendun Ali as his deputies; Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke as overall commander of the four faces of the inner city; Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai as concurrent overall pacifier and suppressor of army and people; Remonstrating Censor and Director of the Close Attendants Bureau, Acting Left and Right Bureau Director of the Branch Secretariat Wugusun Nushen, as concurrent Administrator of Palace Affairs.

units.zh: 又以把撒合為外城東面元帥，術甲咬住南面元帥，崔立西面元帥，孛術魯買奴北面元帥。
units.en: He further appointed Basage marshal of the outer city's eastern sector, Shujia Yaozhu marshal of the south, Cui Li marshal of the west, and Boshulu Mainu marshal of the north.
units.literal: He further made Basage marshal of the east face of the outer city, Shujia Yaozhu marshal of the south, Cui Li marshal of the west, and Boshulu Mainu marshal of the north.

units.zh: 乙酉，除拜定，以京城付之。
units.en: On yiyou day the appointments were finalized, and the capital was entrusted to them.
units.literal: On the day yiyou the appointments were settled, and the capital was entrusted to them.

units.zh: 又以戶部侍郎刁璧為安撫副使，總招撫司，規運京外糧斛。
units.en: He also appointed vice minister of revenue Diao Bi pacification deputy commissioner, in overall charge of the pacification office, to organize the shipment of grain from outside the capital.
units.literal: He also made Vice Minister of Revenue Diao Bi Pacification Deputy Commissioner, in overall charge of the Pacification Office, to plan transport of grain outside the capital.

units.zh: 設講議所，受陳言文字，以大理卿納合德輝、戶部尚書仲平、中京副留守愛失等總其事。
units.en: A deliberation office was set up to receive written submissions, with grand guardian of justice Nahe Dehui, minister of revenue Zhongping, and vice defender of Zhongjing Aishi placed in overall charge.
units.literal: A Deliberation Office was established to receive written submissions; Grand Guardian of Justice Nahe Dehui, Minister of Revenue Zhongping, and Vice Defender of Zhongjing Aishi were placed in overall charge of its affairs.

units.zh: 十二月辛丑，上出京，服絳紗袍，乘馬導從如常儀。
units.en: On xinchou day in the twelfth month the emperor left the capital in a crimson gauze robe, riding out with his usual escort.
units.literal: On the day xinchou in the twelfth month the emperor left the capital, wearing a crimson gauze robe and riding with escort according to the usual ceremony.

units.zh: 留守官及京城父老從至城外奉辭，有詔撫諭，仍以鞭揖之。
units.en: The officials left behind and the elders of the capital followed him outside the walls to bid farewell. He issued an edict of reassurance and still bowed to them with his whip.
units.literal: The officials remaining behind and the elders of the capital followed to outside the walls to take leave; an edict comforted and instructed them, and he still bowed with his whip to them.

units.zh: 速不泬聞上已出，復會兵圍汴。
units.en: When Subutai learned that the emperor had left, he gathered his forces again and renewed the siege of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Subutai, hearing that the emperor had already departed, again gathered troops to besiege Bian.

units.zh: 初，上以東面元帥李辛跋扈出怨言，罷為兵部侍郎，將出，密喻奴申等羈縶之。
units.en: Earlier, because the eastern marshal Li Xin had been insubordinate and voiced complaints, the emperor had demoted him to vice minister of war. Before leaving the city, he secretly told Nushen and the others to detain him.
units.literal: Earlier, because the eastern marshal Li Xin was overbearing and uttered resentful words, the emperor had removed him to Vice Minister of War; as he was about to depart, he secretly instructed Nushen and the others to detain him.

units.zh: 上既行，奴申等召辛，辛懼，謀欲出降，棄馬逾城而走。
units.en: After the emperor had departed, Nushen and the others summoned Li Xin. In fear, Xin plotted to defect, abandoned his horse, and fled over the wall.
units.literal: After the emperor had gone, Nushen and the others summoned Xin; Xin was afraid and plotted to go out and surrender, abandoning his horse and fleeing over the wall.

units.zh: 奴申等遣人追及之，斬於省門。
units.en: Nushen and the others sent men in pursuit, caught him, and beheaded him at the secretariat gate.
units.literal: Nushen and the others sent men in pursuit, overtook him, and beheaded him at the gate of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 汴民以上親出師，日聽捷報，且以二相持重，幸以無事。
units.en: The people of Kaifeng, believing the emperor had gone out to lead the army in person, waited daily for news of victory and trusted that the two chief ministers would keep things secure.
units.literal: The people of Bian, because the emperor had gone out in person with the army, daily awaited reports of victory, and moreover, trusting in the weight of the two councilors, hoped that all would be well.

units.zh: 俄聞軍敗衛州，蒼黃走歸德，民大恐，以為不救。
units.en: Soon word came that the army had been defeated at Weizhou and that the emperor had fled in disarray to Guide. The populace was terrified and believed the city was beyond saving.
units.literal: Before long they heard that the army had been defeated at Weizhou and that he had fled in panic to Guide; the people were greatly afraid and believed there would be no rescue.

units.zh: 時汴京內外不通，米升銀二兩。
units.en: At that time Kaifeng was cut off inside and out, and a sheng of rice sold for two taels of silver.
units.literal: At that time inside and outside Bianjing could not communicate; a sheng of rice cost two taels of silver.

units.zh: 百姓糧盡，殍者相望，縉紳士女多行乞於市，至有自食其妻子者，至於諸皮器物皆煮食之，貴家第宅、市樓肆館皆撤以爨。
units.en: The people ran out of food; corpses of the starved lined the streets; gentry men and women begged in the markets; some even ate their own wives and children; leather goods and utensils of every kind were boiled for food; and the mansions of the wealthy, market towers, and shops were torn down for firewood.
units.literal: The common people exhausted their grain; the dead from starvation lined the roads; gentry and ladies often begged in the markets; there were even those who ate their own wives and children; all sorts of leather goods and utensils were boiled and eaten; mansions of the wealthy and market towers and shops were torn down for fuel.

units.zh: 及歸德遣使迎兩宮，人情益不安，於是民間有立荊王監國以城歸順之議，而二相皆不知也。
units.en: When Guide sent envoys to bring back the empresses, public anxiety deepened. Talk spread among the people of installing Prince Jing as regent and surrendering the city—and neither of the two chief ministers knew of it.
units.literal: When Guide sent envoys to welcome the two palaces, popular sentiment grew still more uneasy; thereupon among the people arose talk of installing Prince Jing as regent and surrendering the city in submission—and the two councilors knew nothing of it.

units.zh: 天興二年正月丙寅，省令史許安國詣講議所言：「古者有大疑，謀及卿士，謀及庶人。
units.en: On bingyin day in the first month of Tianxing 2, secretariat clerk Xu Anguo went to the deliberation office and said: "In antiquity, when grave doubts arose, counsel was sought from ministers and nobles, and from the common people as well.
units.literal: On the day bingyin in the first month of the second year of Tianxing, Secretariat clerk Xu Anguo went to the Deliberation Office and said: "In antiquity, when there was great doubt, counsel was sought from ministers and nobles, and counsel was sought from the common people.

units.zh: 今事勢如此，可集百官及僧道士庶，問保社稷、活生靈之計。」
units.en: Now that matters stand as they do, we should gather officials, monks, Daoists, and commoners alike and ask what plan might preserve the state and save the people."
units.literal: Now that affairs stand thus, we may assemble all officials and monks, Daoists, and commoners, and ask plans for preserving the altars of soil and grain and saving the living people."

units.zh: 左司都事元好問以安國之言白奴申，奴申曰：「此論甚佳，可與副樞議之。」
units.en: Left bureau director Yuan Haowen reported Xu Anguo's proposal to Nushen, who said: "That is an excellent idea. Discuss it with the vice commissioner."
units.literal: Left Bureau Director Yuan Haowen reported Anguo's words to Nushen; Nushen said: "This proposal is excellent; you may discuss it with the Vice Commissioner."

units.zh: 副樞亦以安國之言為然。
units.en: The vice commissioner agreed with Xu Anguo's proposal as well.
units.literal: The Vice Commissioner also considered Anguo's words correct.

units.zh: 好問曰：「自車駕出京，今二十日許，又遣使迎兩宮。
units.en: Haowen said: "It has been about twenty days since the imperial carriage left the capital, and now envoys have again been sent to bring back the empresses.
units.literal: Haowen said: "Since the imperial carriage left the capital, it has been about twenty days, and again envoys have been sent to welcome the two palaces.

units.zh: 民間洶洶，皆謂國家欲棄京城，相公何以處之？」
units.en: The people are in an uproar, all saying the court means to abandon the capital. How do you intend to address this?"
units.literal: Among the people there is uproar; all say the state intends to abandon the capital—how will you, my lords, deal with this?"

units.zh: 阿不曰：「吾二人惟有一死耳。」
units.en: Abu said: "The two of us have nothing but death to offer."
units.literal: Abu said: "We two have only death."

units.zh: 好問曰：「死不難，誠能安社稷、救生靈，死而可也。
units.en: Haowen said: "Death is not difficult. If it would truly save the state and the people, death would be acceptable.
units.literal: Haowen said: "Death is not difficult; if one can truly settle the altars of soil and grain and save the living people, then death is acceptable.

units.zh: 如其不然，徒欲一身飽五十紅衲軍，亦謂之死耶？」
units.en: But if not—if you only want to fill your own bellies while fifty red-cassock guards eat their fill—is that what you call dying?"
units.literal: If it is not so, and one merely wishes to fill one's own belly while fifty red-cassock troops are fed—is that also called death?"

units.zh: 阿不款語曰：「今日惟吾二人，何言不可。」
units.en: Abu said earnestly: "Today it is only the two of us here—what cannot be said openly?"
units.literal: Abu said warmly: "Today it is only we two—what may not be spoken?"

units.zh: 好問乃曰：「聞中外人言，欲立二王監國，以全兩宮與皇族耳。」
units.en: Haowen then said: "I have heard people inside and outside the city say they wish to install a prince as regent, only to preserve the empresses and the imperial clan."
units.literal: Haowen then said: "I have heard people inside and outside say they wish to install the two princes as regents, merely to preserve the two palaces and the imperial clan."

units.zh: 阿不曰：「我知之矣，我知之矣。」
units.en: Abu said: "I know, I know."
units.literal: Abu said: "I know it already, I know it already."

units.zh: 即命召京城官民。
units.en: He immediately ordered officials and commoners of the capital summoned.
units.literal: He at once ordered that officials and people of the capital be summoned.

units.zh: 明日皆聚省中，諭以事勢危急當如之何。
units.en: The next day all gathered at the secretariat, where they were told how to respond to the desperate situation.
units.literal: The next day all assembled in the Secretariat; they were instructed on how to act now that affairs were critically urgent.

units.zh: 有父老七人陳詞云云，二相命好問受其詞。
units.en: Seven community elders presented their statements, and the two chief ministers ordered Haowen to receive them.
units.literal: Seven elders among the fathers of the community presented their statements; the two councilors ordered Haowen to receive their words.

units.zh: 白之奴申，顧曰：「亦為此事也。」
units.en: He reported to Nushen, who turned and said: "So it is about this after all."
units.literal: He reported to Nushen, who looked back and said: "It is also about this matter."

units.zh: 且問副樞「此事謀議今幾日矣」？
units.en: He also asked the vice commissioner: "How many days has this been under discussion?"
units.literal: He also asked the Vice Commissioner, "How many days has this matter been plotted?"

units.zh: 阿不屈指曰：「七日矣。」
units.en: Abu counted on his fingers and said: "Seven days."
units.literal: Abu counted on his fingers and said: "Seven days."

units.zh: 奴申曰：「歸德使未去，慎勿泄。」
units.en: Nushen said: "The envoy from Guide has not yet left. Be careful not to let this out."
units.literal: Nushen said: "The envoy from Guide has not yet departed—take care not to leak this."

units.zh: 或曰是時週邊不解，如在陷阱，議者欲推立荊王以城出降，是亦《春秋》紀季入齊之義，況北兵中已有曹王也。
units.en: Some say that at this time, besieged on every side as if in a trap, those deliberating wished to install Prince Jing and surrender the city—an act in the spirit of Ji Ji's surrender to Qi in the Spring and Autumn Annals—and besides, Prince Cao was already held among the northern forces.
units.literal: Some say that at this time, cut off on every side as if in a trap, those deliberating wished to install Prince Jing and surrender the city—this too was in the sense of Ji Ji of the Spring and Autumn entering Qi; moreover, Prince Cao was already among the northern troops.

units.zh: 眾憤二人無策，但曰死守而已。
units.en: The crowd, furious that the two ministers had no plan, could only cry that they would hold out to the death.
units.literal: The crowd, angry that the two men had no plan, could only say they would die defending to the end.

units.zh: 忽聞召京城士庶計事，奴申拱立無語，獨阿不反復申諭：「國家至此無可奈何，凡有可行當共議之」，且繼以涕泣。
units.en: When the capital's officials and commoners were suddenly summoned to deliberate, Nushen stood with folded hands and said nothing. Abu alone kept repeating: "The state has come to this pass and can do nothing—whatever may yet be done, let us discuss it together," and wept as he spoke.
units.literal: Suddenly they heard that officials and commoners of the capital had been summoned to deliberate; Nushen stood with folded hands and said nothing, while Abu alone repeatedly exhorted: "The state has come to this and can do nothing—whatever may be done, let us discuss it together," and followed with weeping.

units.zh: 明日戊辰，西面元帥崔立與其党孛術魯長哥、韓鐸、藥安國等為變，率甲卒二百橫刀入省中，拔劍指二相曰：「京城危困已極，二公坐視百姓餓死，恬不為慮，何也？」
units.en: The next day, on wuchen day, western marshal Cui Li and his followers Boshulu Changge, Han Duo, Yao Anguo, and others staged a mutiny. Leading two hundred armored soldiers with swords at the ready, they entered the secretariat, drew their blades, and pointed at the two chief ministers: "The capital's plight has reached its limit. You sit by while the people starve to death and show no concern—why?"
units.literal: On the next day, wuchen, the western marshal Cui Li and his partisans Boshulu Changge, Han Duo, Yao Anguo, and others mutinied; leading two hundred armored soldiers with swords drawn across their chests, they entered the Secretariat, drew swords, and pointed at the two councilors, saying: "The capital's peril and distress have reached the limit; you two sit by while the people starve to death and are calmly unconcerned—why?"

units.zh: 二相大駭，曰：「汝輩有事，當好議之，何遽如是。」
units.en: The two ministers were terrified and said: "If you have grievances, let us discuss them properly—why act so rashly?"
units.literal: The two councilors were greatly alarmed and said: "If you have business, it should be discussed properly—why act so hastily?"

units.zh: 立麾其党先殺阿不，次殺奴申及左司郎中納合德輝等，余見《崔立傳》。
units.en: Cui Li signaled his men; they killed Abu first, then Nushen and left bureau director Nahe Dehui and others—the rest is recorded in the Biography of Cui Li.
units.literal: Li waved his partisans on; they first killed Abu, then killed Nushen and Left Bureau Director Nahe Dehui and others—the rest is in the Biography of Cui Li.

units.zh: 劉祁曰：「金自南渡之後，為宰執者往往無恢復之謀，臨事相習低言緩語，互相推讓，以為養相體。
units.en: Liu Qi said: "After the Jin moved south of the river, those who served as chief ministers often had no plan for recovery. When crises arose they spoke in muted, measured tones and deferred to one another, calling it the proper dignity of a councilor.
units.literal: Liu Qi said: "Since the Jin moved south of the river, those who served as chief ministers often had no plans for recovery; when affairs arose they were accustomed to speak in low voices and slow words, deferring to one another, taking this to be cultivating the dignity of a councilor.

units.zh: 每有四方災異、民間疾苦，將奏必相謂曰：'恐聖主心困。
units.en: Whenever there were disasters in the provinces or suffering among the people, before memorializing they would tell one another: 'We must not trouble the emperor's peace of mind.'
units.literal: Whenever there were calamities in the four directions or suffering among the people, before memorializing they would say to one another: 'We fear troubling the sage sovereign's heart.'

units.zh: '事至危處輒罷散，曰'俟再議'，已而複然。
units.en: When matters grew critical they would adjourn, saying 'Let us discuss again later'—and afterward nothing would change.
units.literal: When affairs reached a critical point they would adjourn, saying 'Let us discuss again later'—and afterward it would be the same again.

units.zh: 或有言當改革者，輒以生事抑之，故所用必擇軟熟無鋒芒易制者用之。
units.en: Anyone who urged reform was silenced as a troublemaker, so appointments invariably went to men who were mild, pliable, unremarkable, and easy to control.
units.literal: If anyone spoke of the need for reform, they would suppress it as stirring up trouble; therefore those employed were invariably chosen from the mild, smooth, unedged, and easy to control.

units.zh: 每北兵壓境，則君臣相對泣下，或殿上發長籲而已。
units.en: Whenever northern armies pressed the frontier, emperor and ministers would weep before one another, or let out long sighs in the hall—and do nothing more.
units.literal: Whenever northern troops pressed the borders, ruler and ministers would face one another weeping, or on the palace hall let out long sighs—that was all.

units.zh: 兵退，則大張具，會飲黃閣中矣。
units.en: When the enemy withdrew, they would lay out lavish banquets and feast together in the Yellow Pavilion.
units.literal: When the troops withdrew, they would spread a great feast and drink together in the Yellow Pavilion.

units.zh: 因循苟且，竟至亡國。
units.en: Through procrastination and expedience they brought the state to ruin.
units.literal: Procrastinating and making do, they ultimately brought the state to ruin.

units.zh: 又多取渾厚少文者置之台鼎，宣宗嘗責丞相僕散七斤'近來朝廷紀綱安在'？
units.en: They also favored solid, unlettered men for the highest offices. Emperor Xuanzong once rebuked Chancellor Pushe Qijin: 'Where has the court's discipline gone lately?'
units.literal: They also took many men of solid character but little learning and placed them at the pinnacle of power; Emperor Xuanzong once reproached Chancellor Pushe Qijin: 'Where lately is the court's discipline and order?'

units.zh: 七斤不能對，退謂郎官曰：'上問紀綱安在，汝等自來何嘗使紀綱見我。
units.en: Qijin could not answer. On retiring he told his staff: 'The emperor asks where discipline has gone—you yourselves have never let discipline reach me.'
units.literal: Qijin could not reply; retiring, he said to the bureau officials: 'The emperor asks where discipline and order are—you yourselves have never let discipline and order reach me.'

units.zh: '故正人君子多不見用，雖用亦未久而遽退也。」
units.en: Thus upright men were seldom employed, and even when employed were soon dismissed."
units.literal: Therefore upright gentlemen were mostly not employed; even when employed, they did not long remain before being hurriedly dismissed."

units.zh: 祁字京叔，渾源人。
units.en: Qi, courtesy name Jingshu, was a native of Hunyuan.
units.literal: Qi was styled Jingshu and was a man of Hunyuan.

units.zh: 贊曰：劉京叔《歸潛志》與元裕之《壬辰雜編》二書雖微有異同，而金末喪亂之事猶有足征者焉。
units.en: The encomium says: Liu Jingshu's Returning to Seclusion and Yuan Yuzhi's Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen Year, though they differ in minor details, still provide valuable testimony on the chaos at the end of the Jin.
units.literal: The encomium says: Liu Jingshu's Returning to Seclusion and Yuan Yuzhi's Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen Year, though they differ slightly in places, still offer sufficient testimony concerning the disorders at the end of the Jin.

units.zh: 哀宗北禦，以孤城弱卒托之奴申、阿不二人，可謂難矣。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong went north to resist the invaders, entrusting a besieged city and a feeble garrison to Nushen and Abu alone, the task was formidable indeed.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong went north to resist, entrusting a lone city and weak troops to Nushen and Abu alone, it may be called difficult indeed.

units.zh: 雖然，即墨有安平君，玉壁有韋孝寬，必有以處此。
units.en: Even so, Jimo had Lord Ping of An, and Yubi had Wei Xiaokuan—surely there was a way to meet such a crisis.
units.literal: Even so, at Jimo there was Lord Ping of An, and at Yubi there was Wei Xiaokuan—there must be a way to deal with this.

units.zh: 崔立，將陵人，少貧無行，嘗為寺僧負鈸鼓，乘兵亂從上黨公開為都統、提控，積階遙領太原知府。
units.en: Cui Li was from Jiangling. In youth he was poor and dissolute; he once carried cymbals and drums for temple monks. When the armies fell into chaos he followed Duke Kai of Shangdang as army marshal and military controller, rising in rank to hold the nominal post of prefect of Taiyuan.
units.literal: Cui Li was a man of Jiangling. In youth he was poor and without integrity; he once carried cymbals and drums for temple monks. Taking advantage of the military turmoil, he followed Duke Kai of Shangdang as army marshal and military controller, accumulating rank to hold the nominal post of prefect of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 正大初，求入仕。
units.en: In the early Zhengda era he sought to enter official service.
units.literal: In the early Zhengda era, he sought to enter official service.

units.zh: 為選曹所駁，每以不至三品為恨。
units.en: The personnel selection office rejected him, and he always resented never reaching the third rank.
units.literal: He was rejected by the personnel selection office, and always resented not reaching the third rank.

units.zh: 圍城中授安平都尉。
units.en: Within the besieged city he was appointed commandant of Anping.
units.literal: Within the besieged city he was appointed Commandant of Anping.

units.zh: 天興元年冬十二月，上親出師，授西面元帥。
units.en: In the twelfth month of winter in Tianxing 1, when the emperor personally led troops out, he was appointed western marshal.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in Tianxing 1, when the emperor personally led troops out, he was appointed western marshal.

units.zh: 性淫姣，常思亂以快其欲。
units.en: He was licentious by nature and constantly plotted rebellion to satisfy his desires.
units.literal: His nature was licentious and dissolute; he constantly thought of rebellion to gratify his desires.

units.zh: 藥安國者，管州人，年二十餘，有勇力。
units.en: Yao Anguo was from Guan Prefecture, a little over twenty years old, and known for his courage and strength.
units.literal: Yao Anguo was a man of Guan Prefecture, a little over twenty years of age, brave and strong.

units.zh: 嘗為嵐州招撫使，以罪系開封獄，既出，貧無以為食。
units.en: He had once served as pacification commissioner of Lan Prefecture. Convicted of a crime, he was imprisoned in Kaifeng; after his release he was destitute and without food.
units.literal: He had once been Pacification Commissioner of Lan Prefecture; for a crime he was imprisoned in the Kaifeng jail; after release he was poor and had nothing to eat.

units.zh: 立將為變，潛結納之，安國健啖，日飽之以魚，遂與之謀。
units.en: When Cui Li was planning his mutiny, he secretly recruited Anguo, a hearty eater whom he fed daily on fish until they joined in the plot.
units.literal: When Li was about to mutiny, he secretly won him over; Anguo was a hearty eater, and Li daily fed him his fill with fish, and then plotted with him.

units.zh: 先以家置西城上，事不勝則挈以逃。
units.en: He first stationed his family on the western wall so that if the coup failed he could flee with them.
units.literal: He first placed his family on the western wall of the city; if the affair did not succeed he would take them and flee.

units.zh: 日與都尉楊善入省中候動靜，佈置已定，召善以早食，殺之。
units.en: Each day he entered the secretariat with commandant Yang Shan to watch for developments. Once everything was ready, he invited Shan to an early meal and killed him.
units.literal: Daily he entered the Secretariat with Commandant Yang Shan to watch developments; when arrangements were settled, he summoned Shan for an early meal and killed him.

units.zh: 二年正月，遂帥甲卒二百，撞省門而入。
units.en: In the first month of the second year he led two hundred armored soldiers, smashed through the secretariat gate, and entered.
units.literal: In the first month of the second year he then led two hundred armored soldiers, rammed the Secretariat gate, and entered.

units.zh: 二相聞變趨出，立拔劍曰：「京城危困，二公欲如何處之？」
units.en: The two chief ministers, hearing the disturbance, rushed out. Cui Li drew his sword and said: "The capital is in desperate straits—what do you two intend to do about it?"
units.literal: The two councilors, hearing of the disturbance, hurried out; Li drew his sword and said: "The capital is in peril and distress—how do you two intend to deal with it?"

units.zh: 二相曰：「事當好議之。」
units.en: The two ministers said: "This should be discussed properly."
units.literal: The two councilors said: "The matter should be discussed properly."

units.zh: 立不顧，麾其党張信之、孛術魯長哥出省，二相遂遇害。
units.en: Cui Li paid no heed, signaled his men Zhang Xinzhi and Boshulu Changge, and the two chief ministers were killed.
units.literal: Li paid no heed, waved his partisans Zhang Xinzhi and Boshulu Changge out of the Secretariat, and the two councilors were thereupon killed.

units.zh: 馳往東華門，道遇點檢溫屯阿裏，見其衷甲，殺之。
units.en: He galloped to the Eastern Flowery Gate. On the way he met inspector Wentun Ali, saw armor beneath his robe, and killed him.
units.literal: He galloped to the Eastern Flowery Gate; on the road he met Inspector Wentun Ali, saw that he wore armor beneath his robe, and killed him.

units.zh: 即諭百姓曰：「吾為二相閉門無謀，今殺之，為汝一城生靈請命。」
units.en: He immediately announced to the people: "The two chief ministers shut the gates and had no plan. I have killed them to plead for the lives of everyone in this city."
units.literal: He at once announced to the people: "Because the two councilors shut the gates and had no plan, I have now killed them to plead for the lives of all you people of the city."

units.zh: 眾皆稱快。
units.en: The crowd cheered.
units.literal: The crowd all expressed satisfaction.

units.zh: 是日，御史大夫裴滿阿忽帶、諫議大夫左右司郎中烏古孫奴申、左副點檢完顏阿散、奉禦忙哥、講議蒲察琦、戶部尚書完顏珠顆皆死。
units.en: That day censor-in-chief Peiman Ahudai, remonstrating censor and left and right bureau director Wugusun Nushen, left deputy inspector Wanyan Asan, attendant-in-ordinary Mangge, deliberator Pucha Qi, and minister of revenue Wanyan Zhuke were all killed.
units.literal: That day Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai, Remonstrating Censor and Left and Right Bureau Director Wugusun Nushen, Left Deputy Inspector Wanyan Asan, Attendant-in-Ordinary Mangge, Deliberator Pucha Qi, and Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke all died.

units.zh: 立還省中，集百官議所立。
units.en: Cui Li returned to the secretariat, gathered the officials, and deliberated whom to install as ruler.
units.literal: Li returned to the Secretariat, assembled all officials, and deliberated whom to install.

units.zh: 立曰：「衛紹王太子從恪，其妹公主在北兵中，可立之。」
units.en: Cui Li said: "Prince Congke, son of Emperor Weishao, has a sister the princess held among the northern forces. He should be installed."
units.literal: Li said: "Prince Congke, son of Emperor Weishao, has a sister the princess among the northern troops—he may be installed."

units.zh: 乃遣其党韓鐸以太后命往召從恪。
units.en: He sent his follower Han Duo with the empress dowager's order to summon Congke.
units.literal: He then sent his partisan Han Duo with the empress dowager's order to summon Congke.

units.zh: 須臾入，以太后誥命梁王監國。
units.en: Shortly he arrived, and by the empress dowager's edict Prince Liang was made regent.
units.literal: Before long he entered; by the empress dowager's patent Prince Liang was made regent.

units.zh: 百官拜舞山呼，從恪受之，遂遣送二相所佩虎符詣速不泬納款。
units.en: The officials bowed and shouted their acclamation. Congke accepted the regency and sent the tiger tallies worn by the two chief ministers to Subutai to offer surrender.
units.literal: All officials bowed, danced, and shouted their acclamation; Congke received it, and then sent the tiger tallies worn by the two councilors to Subutai to offer submission.

units.zh: 凡除拜皆以監國為辭。
units.en: All appointments were issued in the regent's name.
units.literal: All appointments and dismissals were issued in the name of the regent.

units.zh: 立自稱太師、軍馬都元帥、尚書令、鄭王，出入禦乘輿，稱其妻為王妃，弟倚為平章政事，侃為殿前都點檢。
units.en: Cui Li styled himself grand preceptor, overall marshal of army and horse, director of the department of state affairs, and prince of Zheng. He rode the imperial carriage, called his wife princess consort, made his younger brother Yi grand councilor, and Kan chief inspector of the palace front.
units.literal: Li styled himself Grand Preceptor, Overall Marshal of Army and Horse, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince of Zheng; he went in and out riding the imperial carriage, called his wife princess consort, made his younger brother Yi Grand Councilor, and Kan Chief Inspector of the Palace Front.

units.zh: 其党孛術魯長哥御史中丞，韓鐸都元帥兼知開封府事，折希顏、藥安國、張軍奴並元帥，師肅左右司郎中，賈良兵部郎中兼右司都事，內府之事皆主之。
units.en: His followers received offices: Boshulu Changge became censor-in-chief; Han Duo overall marshal and concurrent prefect of Kaifeng; Zhe Xiyan, Yao Anguo, and Zhang Junnu all marshals; Shi Su left and right bureau director; Jia Liang bureau director of war and concurrent right bureau director. They controlled all inner palace affairs.
units.literal: His partisans: Boshulu Changge Censor-in-Chief; Han Duo Overall Marshal and concurrent Prefect of Kaifeng; Zhe Xiyan, Yao Anguo, and Zhang Junnu all marshals; Shi Su Left and Right Bureau Director; Jia Liang Bureau Director of War and concurrent Right Bureau Director—all inner palace affairs were under their charge.

units.zh: 初，立假安國之勇以濟事，至是複忌之，聞安國納一都尉夫人，數其違約斬之。
units.en: At first Cui Li had relied on Anguo's courage for the coup, but now he grew jealous. Learning that Anguo had taken a commandant's wife, he accused him of breaking their pact and had him beheaded.
units.literal: At first Li had borrowed Anguo's courage to accomplish the affair; by this time he again envied him, heard that Anguo had taken a commandant's wife, counted it a breach of their agreement, and beheaded him.

units.zh: 壬申，速不泬至青城，立服禦衣，儀衛往見之。
units.en: On renshen day Subutai reached Qingcheng. Cui Li wore imperial robes and went with full ceremonial guard to meet him.
units.literal: On the day renshen Subutai reached Qingcheng; Li wore imperial robes and went with ceremonial guard to see him.

units.zh: 大帥喜，飲之酒，立以父事之。
units.en: The great commander was pleased, offered him wine, and Cui Li treated him with a son's deference.
units.literal: The great commander was pleased, gave him wine to drink, and Li treated him as a father.

units.zh: 既還，悉燒京城樓櫓，火起，大帥大喜，始信其實降也。
units.en: On returning, he burned all the towers and stockades of the capital. When the flames rose, the great commander was delighted and at last believed the surrender was genuine.
units.literal: After returning, he burned all the towers and stockades of the capital; when the fires rose, the great commander was greatly pleased and at last believed he had truly surrendered.

units.zh: 立托以軍前索隨駕官吏家屬，聚之省中，人自閱之，日亂數人猶若不足。
units.en: Cui Li claimed the army needed the families of officials who had accompanied the emperor, gathered them in the secretariat, and examined each in turn. Several people were seized every day, as if that were not enough.
units.literal: Li, on the pretext that the army front demanded the families of officials who had accompanied the emperor, gathered them in the Secretariat; each person was examined in turn, and several people were daily seized in disorder—as if that were not enough.

units.zh: 又禁城中嫁娶，有以一女之故殺數人者。
units.en: He also banned marriages in the city; over a single daughter several people were killed.
units.literal: He also forbade marriage within the city; for the sake of a single daughter several people were killed.

units.zh: 未幾，遷梁王及宗室近族皆置宮中，以腹心守之，限其出入。
units.en: Before long he moved Prince Liang and the nearest members of the imperial clan into the palace, guarded them with trusted men, and restricted their movements.
units.literal: Before long he moved Prince Liang and the close kin of the imperial clan, all placing them in the palace, guarded by trusted men, and restricted their coming and going.

units.zh: 以荊王府為私第，取內府珍玩實之。
units.en: He took Prince Jing's mansion as his private residence and stocked it with treasures from the inner palace.
units.literal: He took Prince Jing's mansion as his private residence and filled it with precious curios from the inner palace.

units.zh: 二月乙酉，以天子袞冕後服上進。
units.en: On yiyou day in the second month he presented the emperor's ceremonial robes and rear garments as tribute.
units.literal: On the day yiyou in the second month he presented the emperor's ceremonial robes and rear garments as tribute.

units.zh: 又括在城金銀，搜索薰灌，訊掠慘酷，百苦備至。
units.en: He also seized all gold and silver in the city, using smoke searches and drenching, interrogation and torture of every cruelty imaginable.
units.literal: He also seized gold and silver within the city, searching with smoke and drenching, interrogating and plundering with cruel severity—every torment was applied.

units.zh: 郕國夫人及內侍高佑、京民李民望之屬，皆死杖下。
units.en: Lady of the State of Cheng, inner attendant Gao You, capital resident Li Minwang, and others all died under the rod.
units.literal: Lady of the State of Cheng, the inner attendant Gao You, the capital resident Li Minwang, and others all died under the cudgel.

units.zh: 溫屯衛尉親屬八人，不任楚毒，皆自盡。
units.en: Eight kinsmen of commandant of the guards Wentun, unable to endure the torture, all killed themselves.
units.literal: Eight kinsmen of the Commandant of the Guards Wentun, unable to endure the torments, all took their own lives.

units.zh: 白撒夫人、右丞李蹊妻子皆被掠死。
units.en: Lady Baisa and the wife and children of right councilor Li Xi were all seized and killed.
units.literal: Lady Baisa and the wife and children of Right Councilor Li Xi were all seized and killed.

units.zh: 同惡相濟，視人如仇，期於必報而後已。
units.en: They aided one another in wickedness, treated people as enemies, and would not rest until every score was settled.
units.literal: Evil men aided one another, treated people as enemies, and would not stop until they had surely repaid every grudge.

units.zh: 人人竊相謂曰：「攻城之後七八日之中，諸門出葬者開封府計之凡百余萬人，恨不早預其數而值此不幸也。」
units.en: People whispered among themselves: "In the seven or eight days after the siege, Kaifeng prefecture counted more than a million bodies carried out for burial at the various gates. We regret not having died then rather than suffer this."
units.literal: People whispered to one another: "In the seven or eight days after the siege, those carried out for burial at the various gates, as counted by the Kaifeng prefecture, totaled more than a million—how we regret not having joined that number earlier and instead meeting this misfortune."

units.zh: 立時與其妻入宮，兩宮賜之不可勝計。
units.en: Cui Li and his wife then entered the palace, where the empresses bestowed gifts beyond counting.
units.literal: Li then entered the palace with his wife; the two palaces bestowed on them gifts beyond counting.

units.zh: 立因諷太后作書陳天時人事，遣皇乳母招歸德。
units.en: Cui Li induced the empress dowager to write describing the situation and sent the imperial wet nurse to summon the court at Guide.
units.literal: Li thereby prompted the empress dowager to write a letter setting forth heaven's seasons and human affairs, and sent the imperial wet nurse to summon Guide.

units.zh: 當時冒進之徒爭援劉齊故事以冀非分者，比肩接武。
units.en: At that time ambitious men citing the precedents of Liu Yu and the Qi state to seek improper rank crowded one after another.
units.literal: At that time those who pressed forward recklessly, each citing the precedents of Liu Yu and Qi to hope for improper rank, stood shoulder to shoulder in succession.

units.zh: 四月壬辰，立以兩宮、梁王、荊王及諸宗室皆赴青城，甲午北行，立妻王氏備仗衛送兩宮至開陽門。
units.en: On renchen day in the fourth month Cui Li sent the empresses, Prince Liang, Prince Jing, and the entire imperial clan to Qingcheng. On jiawu day they departed north. His wife Lady Wang, with full ceremonial guard, escorted the empresses to the Kaiyang Gate.
units.literal: On the day renchen in the fourth month Li sent the two palaces, Prince Liang, Prince Jing, and all members of the imperial clan to Qingcheng; on the day jiawu they went north; Li's wife Lady Wang, with full guard and escort, saw the two palaces to the Kaiyang Gate.

units.zh: 是日，宮車三十七兩，太后先，中宮次之，妃嬪又次之，宗族男女凡五百餘口，次取三教、醫流、工匠、繡女皆赴北。
units.en: That day thirty-seven palace carriages set out—the empress dowager first, then the empress, then the consorts; more than five hundred men and women of the clan followed; then monks, Daoists, Confucians, physicians, artisans, and embroiderers were all taken north.
units.literal: That day there were thirty-seven palace carriages—the empress dowager first, the empress next, consorts after that; men and women of the clan totaled more than five hundred; next were taken the three teachings, medical practitioners, artisans, and embroiderers—all went north.

units.zh: 四月，北兵入城。
units.en: In the fourth month the northern troops entered the city.
units.literal: In the fourth month the northern troops entered the city.

units.zh: 立時在城外，兵先入其家，取其妻妾寶玉以出，立歸大慟，無如之何。
units.en: Cui Li was outside the city at the time. Troops entered his house first, took his wives, concubines, and jewels, and left. When he returned he wept bitterly but could do nothing.
units.literal: Li was then outside the city; troops first entered his house, took his wives, concubines, and jewels, and departed; Li returned and wailed greatly, but could do nothing.

units.zh: 李琦者，山西人，為都尉，在陳州與粘哥奴申同行省事，陳州變，入京，附崔立妹婿折希顏，娶夾谷元之妻，妻年二十余，有姿色，立初拘隨駕官之家屬，妻輿病而往，得免。
units.en: Li Qi was from Shanxi and served as a commandant. At Chen Prefecture he worked with Zhange Nushen as acting branch secretariat director. When Chen mutinied he fled to the capital and attached himself to Cui Li's brother-in-law Zhe Xiyan. He married the wife of Jiagu Yuan, a woman of more than twenty renowned for her beauty. When Cui Li first detained the families of officials who had accompanied the emperor, she went in a litter feigning illness and was spared.
units.literal: Li Qi was a man of Shanxi, a commandant; at Chen Prefecture he served with Zhange Nushen as acting branch secretariat director; when Chen mutinied he entered the capital, attached himself to Cui Li's brother-in-law Zhe Xiyan, and married the wife of Jiagu Yuan—the wife was a little over twenty, with beauty; when Li first detained the families of officials who had accompanied the emperor, the wife went in a litter feigning illness and was spared.

units.zh: 琦娶之後，有言其美者，立欲強之。
units.en: After Qi married her, word of her beauty reached Cui Li, who wished to take her by force.
units.literal: After Qi married her, someone spoke of her beauty; Li wished to take her by force.

units.zh: 琦每見立欲奪人妻，必差其夫遠出，一日差琦出京，琦以妻自隨，如是者再三，立遂欲殺琦。
units.en: Whenever Cui Li coveted another man's wife, he sent the husband away on distant duty. One day he sent Qi out of the capital, but Qi took his wife with him. After this happened several times, Cui Li resolved to kill him.
units.literal: Whenever Qi saw that Li wished to seize another man's wife, Li would surely send the husband far away; one day he sent Qi out of the capital; Qi took his wife with him—this happened again and again—and Li then wished to kill Qi.

units.zh: 琦又數為折希顏所折辱，乃首建殺立之謀。
units.en: Qi had also been repeatedly humiliated by Zhe Xiyan and was the first to propose killing Cui Li.
units.literal: Qi had also repeatedly been humiliated by Zhe Xiyan; he therefore was the first to propose the plot to kill Li.

units.zh: 李伯淵者，寶坻人，本安平都尉司千戶，美姿容，深沉有謀，每憤立不道，欲仗義殺之。
units.en: Li Boyuan was from Baodi, originally a chiliarch in the Anping commandant's office. Handsome and deep-thinking, he constantly resented Cui Li's wickedness and wished to kill him in the name of justice.
units.literal: Li Boyuan was a man of Baodi, originally a chiliarch of the Anping Commandant's office; handsome in bearing, deep and resourceful, he constantly resented Li's wickedness and wished to kill him in the name of righteousness.

units.zh: 李賤奴者，燕人，嘗以軍功遙領京兆府判，壬辰冬，車駕東狩，以都尉權東面元帥。
units.en: Li Jianu was a man of Yan who had once held the distant post of Jingzhao prefect administrator by military merit. In the winter of the renchen year, when the emperor went east on campaign, he served as commandant and acting eastern marshal.
units.literal: Li Jianu was a man of Yan; he had once by military merit held the distant post of Administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture; in the winter of the renchen year, when the imperial carriage went east on campaign, he served as commandant and acting eastern marshal.

units.zh: 立初反，以賤奴舊與敵體，頗貌敬之。
units.en: When Cui Li first rebelled, because Jianu had formerly held rank equal to the enemy's commanders, he treated him with outward respect.
units.literal: When Li first rebelled, because Jianu had formerly been of equal rank with the enemy, he showed him considerable outward respect.

units.zh: 數月之後，勢已固，遂視賤奴如部曲然。
units.en: After several months, once his power was secure, he treated Jianu like a common soldier.
units.literal: After several months his power was secure, and he then treated Jianu like a subordinate soldier.

units.zh: 賤奴積不能平，數出怨言，至是與琦等合。
units.en: Jianu had long been unable to accept this and often voiced complaints. By now he joined with Qi and the others.
units.literal: Jianu long could not be reconciled, often uttered resentful words, and by this time joined with Qi and the others.

units.zh: 三年六月甲午，傳近境有宋軍，伯淵等陽與立謀備禦之策。
units.en: On jiawu day in the sixth month of the third year, word spread that Song troops were near the border. Boyuan and the others pretended to consult with Cui Li on defensive plans.
units.literal: On the day jiawu in the sixth month of the third year, word spread that Song troops were near the borders; Boyuan and the others pretended to deliberate with Li on plans of defense.

units.zh: 翌日晚，伯淵等燒外封丘門以警動立。
units.en: The next evening Boyuan and his men burned the outer Fengqiu Gate to alarm Cui Li.
units.literal: The next evening Boyuan and the others burned the outer Fengqiu Gate to alarm Li.

units.zh: 是夜，立殊不安，一夕百臥起。
units.en: That night Cui Li was extremely uneasy, rising and lying down a hundred times.
units.literal: That night Li was extremely uneasy, rising and lying down a hundred times in one night.

units.zh: 比明，伯淵等身來約立視火，立從苑秀、折希顏數騎往，諭京城民十五以上、七十以下男子皆詣太廟街點集。
units.en: At dawn Boyuan and the others came in person to invite Cui Li to inspect the fire. Cui Li went with Yuan Xiu, Zhe Xiyan, and several horsemen and ordered all men in the capital aged fifteen to seventy to assemble on Taimiao Street for roll call.
units.literal: By dawn Boyuan and the others came in person to invite Li to view the fire; Li followed with Yuan Xiu, Zhe Xiyan, and several horsemen; he ordered all men of the capital from fifteen up to seventy down to assemble for roll call on Taibao Street.

units.zh: 既還，行及梳行街，伯淵欲送立還二王府，立辭數四，伯淵必欲親送，立不疑，倉卒中就馬上抱立。
units.en: On the return, reaching Shuxing Street, Boyuan offered to escort Cui Li back to the Prince of Zheng's mansion. Cui Li declined several times, but Boyuan insisted on escorting him personally. Unsuspecting, Cui Li was embraced on horseback in the sudden move.
units.literal: On returning, as they reached Shuxing Street, Boyuan wished to escort Li back to the Prince of Zheng's mansion; Li declined several times; Boyuan insisted on escorting him personally; Li suspected nothing; in the haste Boyuan embraced Li on horseback.

units.zh: 立顧曰：「汝欲殺我耶？」
units.en: Cui Li looked back and said: "Do you mean to kill me?"
units.literal: Li looked back and said: "Do you wish to kill me?"

units.zh: 伯淵曰：「殺汝何傷。」
units.en: Boyuan said: "What harm is there in killing you?"
units.literal: Boyuan said: "What harm in killing you?"

units.zh: 即出匕首橫刺之，洞而中其手之抱立處，再刺之，立墜馬死。
units.en: He drew a dagger and stabbed across, piercing through his hand where it held Cui Li. He stabbed again, and Cui Li fell from his horse dead.
units.literal: He at once drew a dagger and stabbed across, piercing through to the place where his hand embraced Li; he stabbed again, and Li fell from his horse dead.

units.zh: 伏兵起，元帥黃摑三合殺苑秀。
units.en: Ambush troops rose up, and marshal Huangga Sanhe killed Yuan Xiu.
units.literal: Ambush troops rose; Marshal Huangga Sanhe killed Yuan Xiu.

units.zh: 折希顏後至不知，見立墜馬，謂與人鬥，欲前解之，隨為軍士所斫，被創走梁門外，追斬之。
units.en: Zhe Xiyan arrived later unaware of the plot. Seeing Cui Li fall from his horse, he thought he was fighting someone and tried to intervene. Soldiers hacked him down. Wounded, he fled outside the Liang Gate and was pursued and beheaded.
units.literal: Zhe Xiyan arrived later and did not know; seeing Li fall from his horse, he thought he was fighting with someone and wished to go forward to separate them; he was thereupon hacked by soldiers, wounded, fled outside the Liang Gate, and was pursued and beheaded.

units.zh: 伯淵系立屍馬尾，至內前號於眾曰：「立殺害劫奪，烝淫暴虐，大逆不道，古今無有，當殺之不？」
units.en: Boyuan tied Cui Li's corpse to a horse's tail, came before the inner palace, and shouted to the crowd: "Cui Li murdered, plundered, committed incest, and was violent and tyrannical—treason without parallel in history. Was he not rightly killed?"
units.literal: Boyuan tied Li's corpse to a horse's tail, came before the inner palace, and cried to the crowd: "Li murdered, plundered, committed incest, and was violent and tyrannical—unparalleled treason in past or present—ought he not to have been killed?"

units.zh: 萬口齊應曰：「寸斬之未稱也。」
units.en: Ten thousand voices answered as one: "Death by inch-long cuts would not be punishment enough."
units.literal: Ten thousand mouths answered as one: "Death by inch-long cuts would not be enough."

units.zh: 乃梟立首，望承天門祭哀宗。
units.en: They displayed Cui Li's head on a pole, faced the Gate of Receiving Heaven, and offered sacrifice to Emperor Aizong.
units.literal: They then displayed Li's head on a pole, faced the Gate of Receiving Heaven, and offered sacrifice to Emperor Aizong.

units.zh: 伯淵以下軍民皆慟，或剖其心生啖之。
units.en: From Boyuan down, soldiers and civilians wept; some cut out his heart and ate it raw.
units.literal: From Boyuan down, soldiers and civilians all mourned; some cut out his heart and ate it raw.

units.zh: 以三屍掛闕前槐樹上，樹忽拔，人謂樹有靈，亦厭其為所汙。
units.en: The three corpses were hung on the locust tree before the palace gate. The tree suddenly uprooted itself; people said the tree had a spirit and loathed being defiled by them.
units.literal: The three corpses were hung on the locust tree before the palace gate; the tree suddenly uprooted itself; people said the tree had a spirit and also loathed being defiled by them.

units.zh: 已而有告立匿宮中珍玩，遂籍其家，以其妻王花兒賜丞相鎮海帳下士。
units.en: Before long someone reported that Cui Li had hidden palace treasures. His property was inventoried, and his wife Wang Hua'er was given to a soldier under Chancellor Zhenhai.
units.literal: Before long someone reported that Li had hidden palace treasures; his household goods were then inventoried, and his wife Wang Hua'er was bestowed on a soldier under Chancellor Zhenhai.

units.zh: 初，立之變也，前護衛蒲鮮石魯負祖宗禦容五，走蔡。
units.en: When Cui Li mutinied, former guard Puxian Shilu carried off five imperial portraits of the ancestors and fled to Cai.
units.literal: At the time of Li's mutiny, former guard Puxian Shilu had carried off five imperial portraits of the ancestors and fled to Cai.

units.zh: 前御史中丞蒲察世達、西面元帥把撒合挈其家亦自拔歸蔡。
units.en: Former censor-in-chief Pucha Shida and western marshal Basage also broke out with their families and returned to Cai.
units.literal: Former Censor-in-Chief Pucha Shida and western marshal Basage, taking their families, also broke out and returned to Cai.

units.zh: 七月己巳，以世達為尚書吏部侍郎，權行六部尚書。
units.en: On jisi day in the seventh month Shida was appointed vice minister of personnel of the department of state affairs, acting for the six ministries.
units.literal: On the day jisi in the seventh month Shida was made Vice Minister of Personnel of the Department of State Affairs, acting for the six ministries.

units.zh: 世達嘗為左司郎中，同簽樞密院事，充益政院官，皆稱上意。
units.en: Shida had once served as left bureau director, concurrent signatory of the bureau of military affairs, and officer of the Yizheng Court—all posts in which he had pleased the emperor.
units.literal: Shida had once been Left Bureau Director, concurrent Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and officer of the Yizheng Court—all were said to accord with the emperor's intent.

units.zh: 及上幸歸德，遣世達督陳糧運。
units.en: When the emperor went to Guide, he sent Shida to supervise grain transport from Chen.
units.literal: When the emperor went to Guide, he sent Shida to supervise grain transport from Chen.

units.zh: 陳變，世達亦與脅從，尋間道之汴，至是徒往行在，上念其舊，錄用之。
units.en: When Chen mutinied, Shida was also forced to follow. He soon took a hidden route to Bian and then went to the mobile court. The emperor, recalling his past service, reappointed him.
units.literal: When Chen mutinied, Shida was also coerced to follow; before long he took a hidden route to Bian; by this time he had gone in person to the mobile court; the emperor, recalling his past service, employed him.

units.zh: 左右司官因奏把撒合、石魯亦宜任用，上曰：「世達曲從，非出得已，然朕猶少降資級，以示薄罰。
units.en: The left and right bureau officials memorialized that Basage and Shilu should also be employed. The emperor said: "Shida bent to circumstances—not willingly—yet I still lowered his rank slightly to show a light punishment.
units.literal: The left and right bureau officials thereupon memorialized that Basage and Shilu should also be employed; the emperor said: "Shida bent to follow—not of his own free will—yet I still slightly lowered his rank to show a light punishment.

units.zh: 彼撒合掌軍一面，石魯宿衛九重，崔立之變，曾不聞發一矢，束手於人。
units.en: Basage commanded one sector of the army and Shilu guarded the palace. At Cui Li's mutiny neither loosed a single arrow and both submitted helplessly.
units.literal: Those two—Basage commanding one face of the army, Shilu guarding the ninefold palace—at Cui Li's mutiny never so much as loosed a single arrow and submitted helplessly to others.

units.zh: 今雖來歸，待以不死，足以示恩，又安得與世達等？
units.en: Now that they have returned, sparing their lives is grace enough. How can they be treated like Shida?
units.literal: Now though they have come back, to spare their lives is enough to show grace—how can they be treated like Shida and the others?

units.zh: 撒合老矣，量用其子可也。
units.en: Basage is old; employing his son will suffice.
units.literal: Basage is old; it is enough to employ his son in measure.

units.zh: 石魯但當酬其負禦容之勞。」
units.en: Shilu need only be rewarded for carrying off the imperial portraits."
units.literal: Shilu need only be rewarded for the labor of carrying the imperial portraits."

units.zh: 未幾，以撒合為北門都尉，其子為本軍都統。
units.en: Before long Basage was made commandant of the north gate, and his son commander of the original army.
units.literal: Before long Basage was made Commandant of the North Gate, and his son commander of the original army.

units.zh: 石魯複充護衛。
units.en: Shilu again served as a guard.
units.literal: Shilu again served as guard.

units.zh: 世達字正夫，泰和三年進士。
units.en: Shida, courtesy name Zhengfu, was a jinshi of Taihe 3.
units.literal: Shida was styled Zhengfu and was a Presented Scholar of the third year of Taihe.

units.zh: 論曰：崔立納款，使其封府庫、籍人民以俟大朝之命可也。
units.en: The discussion says: If Cui Li had offered submission, sealed the treasuries, and registered the people while awaiting the Great Court's orders, that would have been acceptable.
units.literal: The discussion says: For Cui Li to offer submission, seal the treasuries, and register the people while awaiting the Great Court's command would have been acceptable.

units.zh: 乘時僭竊，大肆淫虐，征索暴橫，輒以供備大軍為辭，逞欲由己，斂怨歸國，其為罪不容誅矣。
units.en: Instead he seized power, indulged in debauchery and cruelty, extorted with violent arrogance, always citing provision for the great army as his excuse, indulged his own desires, and heaped resentment on the state. His crimes deserved death many times over.
units.literal: Seizing the moment to usurp power, he wantonly committed debauchery and cruelty, levied and seized with violent arrogance, always using provision for the great army as his excuse, indulging his desires as he pleased, gathering resentment upon the state—his crimes could not be punished enough.

units.zh: 而其志方且要求劉豫之事，我大朝豈肯效尤金人者乎！
units.en: Yet he even aspired to the role of Liu Yu. Would our Great Court imitate what the Jin had done!
units.literal: Yet his ambition was even to demand the affair of Liu Yu—would our Great Court imitate the Jin in such a thing!

units.zh: 金俘人之主，帝人之臣，百年之後適啟崔立之狂謀，以成青城之烈禍。
units.en: The Jin had captured another sovereign and made him their subject-emperor. A century later this opened the way for Cui Li's mad plot and the terrible calamity at Qingcheng.
units.literal: The Jin captured another's sovereign and made him emperor their subject; a hundred years later this precisely opened Cui Li's mad plot, to bring about the fierce calamity of Qingcheng.

units.zh: 曾子曰：「戒之戒之，出乎爾者，反乎爾者也。」
units.en: Zengzi said: "Take heed, take heed—what goes out from you returns upon you."
units.literal: Zengzi said: "Take heed, take heed—what goes out from you returns upon you."

units.zh: 豈不信哉！
units.en: How true indeed!
units.literal: Is it not truly so!

units.zh: 聶天驥
units.en: Nie Tianji
units.literal: Nie Tianji

units.zh: 聶天驥，字元吉，五台人。
units.en: Nie Tianji, courtesy name Yuanji, was a native of Wutai.
units.literal: Nie Tianji, styled Yuanji, was a man of Wutai.

units.zh: 至甯元年進士，調汝陰簿，曆睢州司候、封丘令。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhiying 1, was assigned as clerk of Yuyin, and served successively as judicial officer of Sui Prefecture and magistrate of Fengqiu.
units.literal: He was a Presented Scholar in the first year of Zhiying, assigned as clerk of Yuyin, and served in succession as judicial officer of Sui Prefecture and magistrate of Fengqiu.

units.zh: 興定初，辟為尚書省令史。
units.en: At the beginning of Xingding he was recruited as a clerk of the department of state affairs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xingding he was recruited as a clerk of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 時胥吏擅威，士人往往附之，獨天驥不少假借，彼亦不能害也。
units.en: At that time clerks monopolized power and gentlemen often curried favor with them, but Tianji alone would not yield, and they could not harm him.
units.literal: At that time clerks and runners monopolized power; gentlemen often attached themselves to them, but Tianji alone would not yield to them, and they could not harm him either.

units.zh: 尋授吏部主事，權監察御史。
units.en: Before long he was appointed director of the ministry of personnel and acting supervising censor.
units.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Acting Supervising Censor.

units.zh: 夏使賀正旦，互市于會同館，外戚有身貿易於其間者，天驥上章曰：「大官近利，失朝廷體，且取輕外方。」
units.en: When the Xia envoy came for New Year's congratulations, trade was conducted at the Hall of Mutual Accord. A maternal relative of the emperor traded there in person. Tianji memorialized: "High officials pursuing profit disgrace the court and invite contempt from foreign states."
units.literal: When the Xia envoy came to congratulate on New Year's Day, they traded at the Hall of Mutual Accord; a maternal relative personally traded among them; Tianji memorialized: "High officials pursuing profit lose the court's dignity and moreover invite contempt from foreign states."

units.zh: 遂忤太后旨。
units.en: This offended the empress dowager.
units.literal: He thereby offended the empress dowager's intent.

units.zh: 出為同知汝州防禦使事，未赴，陝西行尚書省驛召，特旨遙領金安軍節度副使，兼行尚書省都事。
units.en: He was sent out as associate administrator of the Ru prefecture defense commission but did not take up the post. The Shaanxi branch secretariat summoned him by post relay, and by special edict he held the distant post of vice military commissioner of the Jin'an army and concurrent director of the branch secretariat.
units.literal: He was sent out as Associate Administrator of the Defense Commission of Ru Prefecture but did not take up the post; the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat summoned him by post relay; by special edict he held the distant post of Vice Military Commissioner of the Jin'an Army, concurrent Director of the Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 未幾，人為右司員外郎，轉京兆治中，尋為衛州行尚書六部事。
units.en: Before long he became right bureau vice director, was transferred to Jingzhao administrator, and soon became acting director of the six ministries of the branch secretariat at Wei Prefecture.
units.literal: Before long he entered service as Right Bureau Vice Director, was transferred to Administrator of Jingzhao, and soon became Acting Director of the Six Ministries of the Branch Secretariat at Wei Prefecture.

units.zh: 慶陽圍急，朝廷遣宿州總帥牙古塔救之，以天驥充經歷官。
units.en: When the siege of Qingyang grew urgent, the court sent Suzhou overall commander Yaguta to relieve it, with Tianji as administrative officer.
units.literal: When the siege of Qingyang grew urgent, the court sent the overall commander of Suzhou, Yaguta, to relieve it, with Tianji serving as administrative officer.

units.zh: 圍解，從別帥守邠，帥欲棄州而東，天驥力勸止之，不從，帥坐是被系逮，天驥降京兆治中。
units.en: When the siege was lifted, he followed another commander to hold Bin. The commander wished to abandon the prefecture and flee east. Tianji strongly urged him to stay but was ignored. The commander was arrested, and Tianji was demoted to Jingzhao administrator.
units.literal: When the siege was lifted, he followed another commander to hold Bin; the commander wished to abandon the prefecture and go east; Tianji strongly urged him to stop but was not obeyed; the commander was thereupon arrested and detained; Tianji was demoted to Administrator of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 尋有訟其冤者，即召為開封簽事，旬月複右司員外郎。
units.en: Before long someone petitioned on his behalf. He was summoned as signing officer of Kaifeng and within ten days was again made right bureau vice director.
units.literal: Before long someone petitioned on his behalf that he had been wronged; he was at once summoned as Signing Officer of Kaifeng, and within ten days was again Right Bureau Vice Director.

units.zh: 丁母憂，未卒哭，奪哀複職。
units.en: He entered mourning for his mother, but before the mourning period was complete he was recalled from mourning and restored to office.
units.literal: He mourned his mother; before the mourning rites were completed, he was recalled from mourning and restored to office.

units.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴中。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Kaifeng.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Bian.

units.zh: 崔立變，天驥被創甚，臥一十餘日。
units.en: At Cui Li's mutiny Tianji was severely wounded and lay abed for more than ten days.
units.literal: At Cui Li's mutiny Tianji was severely wounded and lay abed more than ten days.

units.zh: 其女舜英謁醫救療，天驥歎曰：「吾幸得死，兒女曹乃為謁醫，尚欲我活耶？」
units.en: His daughter Shunying went to beg physicians to treat him. Tianji sighed and said: "I was fortunate enough to die—must you children beg physicians? Do you still want me to live?"
units.literal: His daughter Shunying went to beg physicians to save him; Tianji sighed and said: "I was fortunate enough to die—must you children go begging physicians? Do you still want me to live?"

units.zh: 竟鬱鬱以死。
units.en: He ultimately died in grief and distress.
units.literal: He ultimately died in gloom and distress.

units.zh: 舜英葬其父，明日亦自縊，有傳。
units.en: Shunying buried her father; the next day she hanged herself. She has a separate biography.
units.literal: Shunying buried her father; the next day she also hanged herself—there is a separate biography.

units.zh: 天驥沉靜寡言，不妄交。
units.en: Tianji was calm and reserved, spoke little, and did not associate lightly.
units.literal: Tianji was calm and reserved, spoke little, and did not associate lightly.

units.zh: 起於田畝，能以雅道自將，踐曆台省若素宦然，諸人多自以為不及也。
units.en: Rising from humble origins, he conducted himself by refined principles and moved through the high offices as if born to them. Many considered themselves his inferior.
units.literal: Rising from the fields, he could conduct himself by refined principles; passing through the high offices as if a veteran official, many considered themselves his inferior.

units.zh: 赤盞尉忻
units.en: Chizhan Weixin
units.literal: Chizhan Weixin

units.zh: 赤盞尉忻，字大用，上京人。
units.en: Chizhan Weixin, courtesy name Dayong, was a native of Shangjing.
units.literal: Chizhan Weixin, styled Dayong, was a man of Shangjing.

units.zh: 當襲其父謀克，不願就，中明昌五年策論進士第。
units.en: He was to inherit his father's military colony post but declined it and passed the Policy Discourse jinshi examination in Mingchang 5.
units.literal: He was to inherit his father's military colony post but did not wish to; he passed the Presented Scholar examination in Policy Discourse in the fifth year of Mingchang.

units.zh: 後選為尚書省令史、吏部主事、監察御史，言「諸王駙馬至京師和買諸物，失朝廷體。」
units.en: He was later selected as clerk of the department of state affairs, director of the ministry of personnel, and supervising censor, and said: "When princes and imperial sons-in-law come to the capital and forcibly purchase goods, the court loses dignity."
units.literal: Later he was selected as clerk of the Department of State Affairs, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Supervising Censor, and said: "When princes and imperial sons-in-law come to the capital and forcibly purchase goods, the court loses dignity."

units.zh: 有詔禁止。
units.en: An edict forbade the practice.
units.literal: An edict forbade it.

units.zh: 遷鎮南軍節度副使、息州刺史。
units.en: He was transferred to vice military commissioner of the Zhennan army and prefect of Xi Prefecture.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army and Prefect of Xi Prefecture.

units.zh: 耕鞠場種禾，兩禾合穗，進於朝，特詔褒諭。
units.en: He planted grain on the cuju field, and two stalks joined in one ear. He presented this to the court and received a special edict of praise.
units.literal: He planted grain on the cuju field; two stalks joined in one ear; he presented it to the court, and a special edict praised and commended him.

units.zh: 改丹州，遷鄭州防禦使，權許州統軍使。
units.en: He was moved to Dan Prefecture, promoted to defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, and made acting overall commander of Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: He was moved to Dan Prefecture, promoted to Defense Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, and Acting Overall Commander of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 丞相高汝礪嘗薦其才可任宰相。
units.en: Chancellor Gao Rulue once recommended him as fit for the chancellorship.
units.literal: Chancellor Gao Rulue once recommended that his talent was fit for the chancellorship.

units.zh: 元光二年正月，召為戶部侍郎。
units.en: In the first month of the second year of Yuanguang he was summoned as vice minister of revenue.
units.literal: In the first month of the second year of Yuanguang he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 未幾，權參知政事。
units.en: Before long he was made acting vice grand councilor.
units.literal: Before long he was Acting Vice Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 二月，為戶部尚書，權職如故。
units.en: In the second month he became minister of revenue while retaining his acting duties.
units.literal: In the second month he became Minister of Revenue, his acting duties remaining as before.

units.zh: 三月，拜參知政事，兼修國史。
units.en: In the third month he was appointed vice grand councilor and concurrent compiler of the national history.
units.literal: In the third month he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and concurrent Compiler of the National History.

units.zh: 詔諭近臣曰：「尉忻資稟純質，事可倚任，且其性孝，朕今相之，國家必有望，汝輩當效之也。」
units.en: An edict told the close ministers: "Weixin's character is pure and solid and he may be relied upon in affairs. Moreover he is filial. I now make him councilor—the state must have hope. You should take him as your model."
units.literal: An edict instructed the close ministers: "Weixin's endowment is pure and solid; in affairs he may be relied upon, and moreover his nature is filial. I now make him councilor—the state must have hope; you should take him as your model."

units.zh: 正大元年五月，拜尚書右丞。
units.en: In the fifth month of Zhengda 1 he was appointed right vice director of the department of state affairs.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhengda he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 哀宗欲修宮室，尉忻極諫，至是臥薪嚐膽為言，上悚然從之。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong wished to repair the palace buildings, Weixin remonstrated fiercely, even invoking the example of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall. The emperor was startled and complied.
units.literal: Emperor Aizong wished to repair the palace buildings; Weixin remonstrated to the utmost, even speaking of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall; the emperor was startled and complied.

units.zh: 同判睦親府內族撒合輦交結中外，久在禁近。
units.en: Associate administrator of the Muxin princely establishment, inner clansman Sagelian, cultivated connections throughout the court and had long been in the inner circle.
units.literal: Associate Administrator of the Muxin Princely Establishment, Inner Clansman Sagelian, cultivated connections inside and outside the court and had long been in the inner circle.

units.zh: 哀宗為太子，有定策功，由是頗惑其言，複倚信日深，台諫每以為言。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, Sagelian had helped settle the succession. For this reason the emperor was much swayed by his words and relied on him ever more deeply. The censorate often remonstrated about this.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, he had the merit of settling the succession; for this reason he was much swayed by his words, and reliance and trust grew daily deeper; the censorate often spoke of it.

units.zh: 太后嘗戒敕曰：「上之騎鞠舉樂，皆汝教之，再犯必杖汝。」
units.en: The empress dowager once admonished him: "The emperor's riding, cuju, and music—all were taught by you. Offend again and you will be beaten."
units.literal: The empress dowager once admonished him: "The emperor's riding, cuju, and music—all were taught by you; if you offend again you will surely be beaten."

units.zh: 哀宗終不能去。
units.en: In the end Emperor Aizong could not remove him.
units.literal: Emperor Aizong in the end could not remove him.

units.zh: 尉忻諫曰：「撒合輦奸諛之最，日在天子左右，非社稷福。」
units.en: Weixin remonstrated: "Sagelian is the worst of flatterers and sycophants. Day after day he is at the emperor's side. This is no blessing to the state."
units.literal: Weixin remonstrated: "Sagelian is the worst of flatterers and sycophants; day by day at the Son of Heaven's side—this is no blessing to the altars of soil and grain."

units.zh: 上悔悟，出為中京留守，朝論快之。
units.en: The emperor repented and sent him out as defender of Zhongjing, to the satisfaction of court opinion.
units.literal: The emperor repented and came to his senses; he sent him out as Defender of Zhongjing, and court opinion rejoiced.

units.zh: 五年，致仕，居汴中，崔立之變明日，召家人付以後事，望睢陽慟哭，以弓弦自縊而死，時年六十三。
units.en: In the fifth year he retired and lived in Kaifeng. The day after Cui Li's mutiny he summoned his family, entrusted them with his final affairs, looked toward Suiyang and wept bitterly, then hanged himself with a bowstring. He was sixty-three.
units.literal: In the fifth year he retired and lived in Bian; on the day after Cui Li's mutiny he summoned his family, entrusted them with his final affairs, looked toward Suiyang and wailed in grief, and hanged himself with a bowstring; he was then sixty-three years old.

units.zh: 一子名董七，沒於兵間。
units.en: He had one son named Dongqi, who perished in the warfare.
units.literal: One son named Dongqi perished amid the warfare.

units.zh: 弟秉甫，字正之。
units.en: His younger brother Bingfu, courtesy name Zhengzhi.
units.literal: His younger brother Bingfu was styled Zhengzhi.

units.zh: 贊曰：聶天驥素履清慎，赤盞尉忻天資忠諒，在治世皆足為良臣，不幸仕亂離之朝，以得死為願欲，哀哉！
units.en: The encomium says: Nie Tianji lived with purity and caution; Chizhan Weixin was loyal and sincere by nature. In an age of peace both would have been fine ministers. Unhappily they served a court torn by chaos and took death as their dearest wish. How lamentable!
units.literal: The encomium says: Nie Tianji in his conduct was pure and cautious; Chizhan Weixin by nature was loyal and sincere—in an age of good government both would have been sufficient as fine ministers; unhappily they served a court of chaos and separation, and took death itself as their wish—how lamentable!
